textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · House of Hundreds - II · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Numbers can be shown with tiles or blocks of hundreds, tens and ones. Eight hundred thirty-two is 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 2 ones. A number like 504 has 5 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Numbers can be shown with tiles or blocks of hundreds, tens and ones. Eight hundred thirty-two is 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 2 ones. A number like 504 has 5 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones. The zero tells us there are no tens.
beats.speakEn: Numbers can be shown with tiles or blocks of hundreds, tens and ones. Eight hundred thirty-two is 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 2 ones. A number like 504 has 5 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones. The zero tells us there are no tens.

beats.en: On a number line, find the tens, fifties or hundreds marks on either side of a number. The number may land exactly on a mark. 468 lies between 400 and 500, between 450 and 500, and between 460 and 470.
beats.speakEn: On a number line, find the tens, fifties or hundreds marks on either side of a number. The number may land exactly on a mark. 468 lies between 400 and 500, between 450 and 500, and between 460 and 470.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · House of Hundreds - II · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: The same number can be made in many ways. 368 is 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones, and it is also 300 + 60 + 8. 368 is also 68 more than 300, and it is 32 less than 400, because 400 - 32 = 368.

beats.en: The same number can be made in many ways. 368 is 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones, and it is also 300 + 60 + 8. 368 is also 68 more than 300, and it is 32 less than 400, because 400 - 32 = 368.
beats.speakEn: The same number can be made in many ways. 368 is 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones, and it is also 300 + 60 + 8. 368 is also 68 more than 300, and it is 32 less than 400, because 400 - 32  equals  368.

beats.en: With the digits 3 and 8 we can make 2-digit numbers such as 33, 38, 83 and 88 and 3-digit numbers such as 338, 383, 388, 833, 838 and 883, if digits can repeat.
beats.speakEn: With the digits 3 and 8 we can make 2-digit numbers such as 33, 38, 83 and 88 and 3-digit numbers such as 338, 383, 388, 833, 838 and 883, if digits can repeat.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · House of Hundreds - II · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: In Bhutasankhya, which means word numerals, a word stands for a number. The Moon stands for 1 because there is one Moon, Eyes stand for 2, Hexagon for 6 and a Palm for 5 fingers.
